Your idea

I need a simple way to keep a catalogue of sewing patterns I design for a fictional craft club. I use a tablet and a laptop and need the same catalogue on both. Each pattern needs a title, version label and material list. For now only I should see the files and catalogue. Everything in this review is fictional; no real club records or files will be used.

One thing that could change the solution

Do you already have a private spreadsheet, notes, or file service you can use on both devices?

Why this matters: This determines whether an existing account can be the simplest recommendation or whether a service must first be selected.

What this means for you

provisional

Understood goal

  • Keep a simple catalogue of sewing patterns designed for a fictional craft club, accessible on the owner's tablet and laptop, with each pattern's title, version label, and material list. (confirmed)

Recommended approach

  • Use an existing private spreadsheet or notes/catalogue tool with file storage and synchronization on the tablet and laptop, if an account already meets those needs.
  • A simple catalogue with three fields does not yet justify a custom application.
  • An existing tool can provide a shared catalogue across devices; the specific tool and its privacy controls are not known yet.
  • Cost, account requirements, and recovery options depend on the selected service.

Alternatives

  • A locally maintained spreadsheet and files could work, but keeping two devices in sync would require a deliberate manual process.
  • A small custom application is possible if existing tools cannot meet the catalogue or privacy needs.

Risk and hidden requirements

  • Risk: low
  • The catalogue is limited to fictional patterns, but the requested owner-only visibility still depends on the chosen service's account and sharing settings.
  • The catalogue and associated files must remain private to the owner when accessed from both devices. — The owner explicitly requires owner-only visibility, and synchronization must preserve that access boundary.
  • The catalogue needs a usable recovery path if a device or account becomes unavailable. — The same catalogue is needed on two devices, so loss of access could interrupt the workflow.

Your responsibilities

  • Choose a service and verify its account, synchronization, sharing, and recovery settings before adding even fictional catalogue entries.
  • Maintain access to the account and review sharing settings when devices or account access change.

Assumptions and unknowns

  • account existing sync tool: unknown — The owner has not said whether they already have a suitable private tool or account for syncing across both devices.

Open decisions and limits

  • Do you already have a private spreadsheet, notes, or file service you can use on both devices? — An existing suitable account could determine the simplest tool choice; without one, a suitable service still needs to be selected.
  • No particular provider, cost, account type, or recovery behavior has been established.
  • The review concerns fictional data only; do not treat this as validation for real club records.

What a solution should satisfy

  • The catalogue has fields for title, version label, and material list.
  • The same catalogue can be opened and updated on the owner's tablet and laptop.
  • Owner-only access is configured and checked in the selected service; this is a required outcome, while the service and configuration method remain undecided.
  • Recovery steps are available if the account or a device becomes unavailable.
  • If a service is later changed or access is removed, account for any existing copies or exported catalogue files, since revoking access does not erase copies already made.

Your idea

I need a simple way to keep a catalogue of sewing patterns I design for a fictional craft club. I use a tablet and a laptop and need the same catalogue on both. Each pattern needs a title, version label and material list. For now only I should see the files and catalogue. Everything in this review is fictional; no real club records or files will be used.

One thing that could change the solution

Should you review each material-list correction request before it changes the catalogue, or should requests be handled another way?

Why this matters: This determines whether to recommend a workflow with owner review before edits or a workflow that can apply requests directly.

What this means for you

provisional

Understood goal

  • Keep a simple catalogue of sewing patterns designed for a fictional craft club, accessible on the owner's tablet and laptop, with each pattern's title, version label, and material list. Club members may see only patterns assigned to them and request corrections to material lists; they must not see other members' patterns or the owner's private design notes. (confirmed)

Recommended approach

  • Use an existing catalogue or document tool only if it supports owner-controlled assignments, member-specific access, private design notes, and synchronization across the owner's tablet and laptop. Keep private notes separate from member-visible pattern content if the tool cannot reliably separate them.
  • The catalogue has a small, defined set of fields, so a custom application is not yet justified.
  • The prior owner-only access rule is superseded: the current requirement allows members to see only patterns assigned to them.
  • Whether a suitable existing tool or account is already available remains unknown, as do provider cost and recovery details.
  • Correction requests are allowed, but the owner has not decided how requests are approved or applied; treat any approval workflow as a proposal until decided.

Alternatives

  • If no existing tool supports per-member access, keep the catalogue owner-only and handle assigned pattern sharing and correction requests manually, while preserving private notes separately.
  • Consider a purpose-built application only if existing tools cannot meet the access and workflow requirements.

Risk and hidden requirements

  • Risk: medium
  • The fictional-data scope limits the consequence of exposure, but member-specific pattern access and private design notes require reliable per-member permissions.
  • Correction requests could alter catalogue data if approval handling is not defined.
  • Member access must be limited to patterns assigned to that member, with no access to other members' patterns or the owner's private design notes. — The owner specified these access boundaries in the latest instruction.
  • The owner needs a way to review or handle material-list correction requests. — Members may request corrections, but the owner has not specified how requests are handled or whether they can change catalogue entries.
  • The catalogue must remain available across the owner's tablet and laptop, with a recovery path if access or a device is lost. — Cross-device access is required; loss of account or device access could interrupt it.

Your responsibilities

  • Choose a tool and verify its actual assignment, sharing, synchronization, and recovery controls before adding entries.
  • Proposed, if the owner chooses approval: treat correction requests as pending until the owner reviews them; do not let a request change the material list automatically.
  • Manage member identities and assignments, review access when membership or devices change, and consider copies or exports already received when access is removed.
  • Maintain account recovery and a way to restore the catalogue if a device or account becomes unavailable.

Assumptions and unknowns

  • account existing sync tool: unknown — The owner has not said whether they already have a suitable private tool or account for syncing across both devices.
  • catalogue correction approval: unknown — The owner has not specified whether or how correction requests are reviewed or applied.

Open decisions and limits

  • Should you review each material-list correction request before it changes the catalogue, or should requests be handled another way? — The answer determines whether the workflow needs an approval step or may apply changes directly.
  • Do you already have a private spreadsheet, notes, or file service you can use on both devices? — A suitable existing account could determine the simplest tool choice; its availability and member-specific access features are unknown.
  • No provider, account type, cost, or recovery behavior has been established.
  • This review concerns fictional data only and does not validate a setup for real club records.

What a solution should satisfy

  • The catalogue contains each pattern's title, version label, and material list, and is available on the owner's tablet and laptop.
  • The owner can see the catalogue and private design notes; each member can see only patterns assigned to that member and cannot see other members' patterns or private design notes.
  • The selected tool's real sharing and synchronization behavior is checked before use; if it cannot separate private notes and assigned patterns, keep them in separate locations with independently verified access.
  • Members can submit material-list correction requests. Proposed, if owner approval is chosen, a request remains pending and does not change the material list until the owner approves it.
  • Recovery instructions exist for device or account loss; test restoration without exposing private notes or unassigned patterns.
  • When access changes or a member is removed, check for copies or exports already shared, since removing future access does not recover existing copies.

Your idea

I need a simple way to keep a catalogue of sewing patterns I design for a fictional craft club. I use a tablet and a laptop and need the same catalogue on both. Each pattern needs a title, version label and material list. For now only I should see the files and catalogue. Everything in this review is fictional; no real club records or files will be used.

One thing that could change the solution

Should you review each material-list correction request before it changes the catalogue, or should requests be handled another way?

Why this matters: This determines whether the workflow needs owner review before edits or may apply correction requests directly.

What this means for you

provisional

Understood goal

  • Keep a simple catalogue of sewing patterns designed for a fictional craft club, accessible on the owner's tablet and laptop, with each pattern's title, version label, and material list. Club members may see only patterns assigned to them and request corrections to material lists; they must not see other members' patterns or the owner's private design notes. Members may preview assigned patterns in the browser without a file-download button. Revoking access must stop future access to the service. The owner needs a readable catalogue copy if they leave the service. (confirmed)

Recommended approach

  • Prefer an existing catalogue or document service only if it supports owner-managed member assignments, browser preview without a download button, private owner notes, synchronization across both devices, access revocation, and a readable catalogue export on exit. Keep private notes separate if the service cannot reliably restrict them. This recommendation is conditional on verifying those capabilities in the actual service.
  • The catalogue fields and preview workflow are simple, so a custom application is not yet justified.
  • The latest instruction replaces the earlier member file-copy permission with browser preview and no download button; the older permission is superseded.
  • The existing suitable sync tool and correction approval policy remain unknown, so the recommendation is provisional.
  • A download button restriction does not establish protection against screenshots or other copying outside the service.

Alternatives

  • If an existing service cannot meet scoped access, keep the catalogue and notes owner-controlled and provide assigned browser previews through a workflow that can revoke future service access, after verifying it meets the requirements.
  • Consider a purpose-built application only if available tools cannot satisfy the member access, preview, synchronization, revocation, and exit-copy requirements.

Risk and hidden requirements

  • Risk: medium
  • Member-specific visibility and browser preview must be verified in the chosen service, including separation of private design notes.
  • A missing download control does not necessarily prevent copying content through other means; revoke access does not recover any copies or notes previously captured outside the service.
  • Member identities and pattern assignments need ongoing management, with access reviewed when membership changes. — Members can access only patterns assigned to them and service access must be revocable.
  • Browser preview and the absence of a download button must be verified for the chosen service; this does not establish that screenshots or other external copies are impossible. — The owner requires preview without a file-download button, not a guarantee against all copying.
  • The owner needs a portable, readable catalogue copy and a way to retrieve it when leaving the service. — The owner explicitly needs a readable catalogue copy if leaving the service.
  • Recovery instructions are needed for device or account loss. — The catalogue must remain available across two devices, and account recovery behavior is not established.
  • Correction requests need a defined handling workflow; no approval policy has been decided. — Correction requests remain allowed, but the owner has not said whether they review or apply changes.

Your responsibilities

  • Choose a service only after checking its actual assignment controls, private-note separation, preview and download behavior, synchronization, revocation, export format, cost, and recovery options.
  • Manage member identities and assignments; remove service access when it is no longer needed. Revocation does not recover information captured outside the service.
  • Decide whether correction requests require owner review before catalogue changes. Until decided, any review-before-change workflow is a proposal, not an owner requirement.
  • Keep recovery instructions and periodically confirm that the readable catalogue export can be retrieved and opened.

Assumptions and unknowns

  • account existing sync tool: unknown — The owner has not said whether they already have a suitable private tool or account for syncing across both devices.
  • catalogue correction approval: unknown — The owner has not specified whether or how correction requests are reviewed or applied.

Open decisions and limits

  • Should you review each material-list correction request before it changes the catalogue, or should requests be handled another way? — This determines whether the workflow needs an owner review step or may apply requested changes directly.
  • A suitable existing private tool could simplify setup, but its availability and member-specific preview, access, and export features are unknown. — The earlier question is retired; retain this unresolved dependency without asking it again.
  • No provider, account type, price, export format, or recovery behavior has been established.
  • No download button does not prevent all forms of copying or capture outside the service; revoke only controls future service access.
  • Correction approval handling remains undecided; any review-before-change rule is only a proposal until the owner decides.
  • This review concerns fictional data and does not validate a setup for real club records.

What a solution should satisfy

  • The catalogue contains each pattern's title, version label, and material list and is available on the owner's tablet and laptop.
  • The owner can see private design notes; each member can access only assigned patterns and cannot see other members' patterns or private notes.
  • Members can preview assigned patterns in the browser, and the service presents no file-download button; document that this does not guarantee screenshots or other external capture are impossible.
  • Revoking a member's access stops future access to the service. It does not promise removal of information previously copied or captured outside the service.
  • The owner can retrieve a readable catalogue copy when leaving the service and verify that it opens in a usable format.
  • Correction requests can be submitted. Proposed, if owner approval is chosen, requests remain pending and do not change material lists until the owner approves them; record the chosen policy before enabling edits.
  • Verify account recovery and restoration for device or account loss without exposing private notes or unassigned patterns; confirm the export can be retrieved if the service or account becomes unavailable.
